messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: Dedicated capacity reservation 'eu-west-3-resv-42' queue length > 1200 for 7m, throttle rate triggered, impacted tenants: 3. Priority: P1. @oncall
Maya: i'm looking. dashboards show steady arrival rate + one tenant with huge spike. autoscaler requests pending, API to add GPUs returning 429 from allocation service.
Sanjay: sounds like the reserved pool got oversubscribed by a single tenant job burst. I see a bunch of long-running sessions from tenant 'thermotech-inc' pinned to reserved instances.
Maya: confirming noisy neighbor. their job starts around 14:06 UTC and never releases the kv cache — token churn is huge. queue growth at worker-proxy layer. latency > 2.5s for all dedicated routes.
Julia: is this the autoscaler limit we've seen before? any cloud quota errors in logs?
Maya: yes, allocation API shows "scale_limit_reached" and cloud quota soft-limit on region GPUs (we're close to reserved cap for this dedicated pool).
Kevin: can we evict or throttle that tenant's sessions? they have reserved capacity paid but too noisy.
Sanjay: we cannot evict reserved instances directly, but we can apply per-tenant concurrency throttles at the routing layer and reduce their max workers. that should free the queue for others.
Maya: rolling out a policy patch to route-service now: set `max_concurrency=4` for tenant thermotech-inc and `priority=high` for enterprise tenants with active reservations.
Maya: applying patch:
```
curl -X POST https://routing.internal/api/tenants/thermotech-inc/policy \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ROUTE_ADMIN' \
  -d '{"max_concurrency":4, "burst_allowance":2}'
```
incident-bot: deploy started (deploy-8723) — will stream logs here.
Julia: also kicking autoscaler manual-scale request: `POST /admin/pools/eu-west-3/resv-42/scale?delta=4` — but alloc service already 429'd.
Kevin: if cloud quota is the bottleneck, manual scale will fail. need SRE to request temporary quota bump or move some capacity to a different dedicated pool.
Maya: i'm going to drain idle reserved slots from non-enterprise test tenants to free 2 GPUs temporarily. initiating drain: `infractl drain --pool resv-42 --count 2 --reason noisy-tenant-mitigation`
Sanjay: good. also enabling prefix KV cache eviction for thermotech's sessions to reduce memory pressure: `config update` pushed.
Alice-CS: looping in CS. i'm notifying thermotech support immediately and asking them to pause large batch jobs. message drafted:
"Hi Thermotech — we are seeing unusually high sustained usage on your reserved capacity. We are throttling concurrency temporarily to protect other tenants. Can you pause large batch jobs for 30m while we mitigate? — Alice, CS"
Alice-CS: sent. they acknowledged, checking with engineering to pause on their side.
Maya: drain completed, freed 2 GPUs. route queue length dropping from 1200 -> 480 in 6m. latency returning to ~800ms for routed requests.
incident-bot: deploy-8723 completed. routing policy updated for thermotech-inc.
Sanjay: what's left on the backend? autoscaler logs show 3 pending allocation ops failing with `QuotaExceeded` from cloud provider.
Kevin: i'll open a ticket with cloud support for a temporary quota increase in eu-west-3. ETA uncertain. in parallel, can we take some tenants to eu-west-1 dedicated pool as a fallback?
Maya: yes, we have cross-pool routing. spinning up a small routing rule to route low-priority resv requests to eu-west-1 fallback. patching now.
Maya: applied fallback; low-priority queues draining to eu-west-1. high-priority enterprise requests still served in eu-west-3.
Julia: customer impact: thermotech affected (throttled), 2 other enterprise tenants experienced elevated latency (SLA risk but no error rates increase beyond 0.5%). marking incident impact as limited.
Kevin: notifying account reps for the two impacted customers and creating incident page in status.redwood.ai.
Alice-CS: notified them and included mitigation steps + timeline. thermotech willing to pause for 22 minutes and then test staged jobs.
Maya: notes for postmortem: (1) autoscaler didn't surface quota limit early, (2) no auto-throttle for reserved tenants, (3) routing had one-click mitigation but needed manual drain and CS coordination.
Sanjay: action items: create per-reservation noisy-tenant detectors + auto-shutdown of runaway sessions; add quota preflight checks to autoscaler; add a soft isolation policy when reservation queue > 80%.
Maya: assigning follow-ups: SRE (Kevin) -> cloud quota request + fallback automation; Infra (Sanjay) -> auto-throttle implementation; Product (Julia) -> update runbook for reserved tenant mitigation; CS (Alice-CS) -> follow up with thermotech on job scheduling best practices.
incident-bot: PAGER: incident acknowledged. Incident channel created: #inc-1794501123-reservation-oversubscribe. Runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/reservation-noisy-tenant
Maya: handing off to Kevin for overnight monitoring. i'll update the runbook and start a short blameless postmortem doc.
Kevin: ack. i'll monitor queue metrics and cloud ticket. ping me if queue > 600 again.
Alice-CS: closing loop with thermotech; they confirmed tests passed after throttling, will adopt smaller batch windows.
Maya: bringing incident to mitigated state. queue at 120 now, latency stabilized. moving to post-incident review.
Sanjay: thanks team.
